ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF) Articles L561-1 to L561-60 and R561-1 to R561-60-3 (AML/CFT customer due diligence, beneficial-owner identification, TRACFIN reporting and asset-freeze measures); Article L561-2-2 and R561-2-1 et seq. incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code, Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 and R.227-1 et seq. for the Société par Actions Simplifiée; Articles L.123-1 et seq. and R.123-1 et seq. for registration in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés; Articles L.561-46 et seq. for beneficial ownership filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent local Registry of the Commercial Court (Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce) through the national Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic declaration of creation of a company filed through the Guichet unique, supported by executed SAS articles of association, capital deposit certificate, publication notice, and beneficial ownership declaration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital applies to an SAS. At least 50% of cash contributions must be paid upon incorporation, with the balance payable within five years of registration. Cash contributions must be deposited with an authorized bank, notary, or Caisse des Dépôts before filing, and the deposit certificate must be submitted. Contributions in kind require valuation by a commissaire aux apports unless the statutory exemption conditions are satisfied.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accept the subscription of all shares stated in the articles of association and acknowledge payment of the required portion of each cash contribution, subject to the capital deposit certificate. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at [full French address], effective upon registration. RESOLVED, that [name] be appointed Président for the statutory term and granted the powers provided by law and the articles of association. RESOLVED, that [name] be appointed Directeur Général, if applicable, with the authority specified in the articles. The officers are authorized to complete all incorporation, registry, tax, banking, and beneficial ownership formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Execute SAS Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company founders, legal counsel, and the appointed registered-office provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare French-language articles specifying the corporate name, purpose, registered office, duration, share capital, classes of shares, transfer restrictions, governance, Président powers, financial year, and dissolution rules. Obtain signatures from all subscribers. Use qualified electronic signatures where accepted. Notarization is generally not required for ordinary cash contributions; notarized instruments are required where real estate or other legally protected assets are contributed.
required_dossiers: Share subscription and capital contribution schedule
Identity documents for founders, officers, and legal representatives
Proof of address for each individual officer
Corporate extracts and authority documents for corporate shareholders
Power of attorney, if a filing agent is used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct defective clauses, obtain missing signatures, replace unacceptable address evidence, and re-execute or electronically sign the affected documents before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized French bank, notary, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital account in the name of the company being formed. Transfer the subscribed cash capital and provide the executed articles, subscription schedule, founder identification, beneficial ownership information, and source-of-funds evidence requested under customer due diligence rules. Obtain the certificate of deposit and retain the bank confirmation for the Guichet unique filing.
required_dossiers: Draft or executed articles of association
Business plan or activity description if requested by the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to bank compliance queries with ownership, source-of-funds, and business-purpose evidence. If the bank declines onboarding, obtain the deposit certificate from another authorized institution or a notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal habilité à recevoir des annonces légales et judiciaires in the registered-office department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a statutory incorporation notice containing the company name, legal form, capital, registered office, purpose, duration, Président identity and address, and registration details where applicable. Pay the regulated publication charge and obtain the attestation de parution. The notice must be published before the creation filing is submitted.
required_dossiers: Identity and address of the Président
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request a corrected notice or correction notice from the authorized journal and upload the corrected attestation with the filing. Reconcile all particulars exactly with the articles and filing form.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Creation and Beneficial Ownership Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises; processing Registry of the Commercial Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic creation declaration, upload the articles, capital deposit certificate, publication attestation, registered-office evidence, officer declarations, and beneficial ownership information. Declare the principal activity consistently with the corporate purpose. Pay the applicable registration and beneficial ownership charges. Use the electronic filing receipt to monitor queries and retain the final Kbis extract.
required_dossiers: Non-conviction and filiation declarations for legal representatives
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer a registry deficiency notice through the Guichet unique within the stated deadline, upload corrected documents, and pay any additional charge. If rejected, file a corrected application; judicial remedies may be available against a formal refusal before the competent court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Activate Corporate Operations and Governance Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company officers, commercial bank, tax administration, and relevant social-security portals
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, obtain the definitive Kbis, request release of the capital account, open the operating bank account, maintain the share-transfer register and beneficial ownership records, and adopt the first shareholder or board resolution. Register for VAT and corporate tax administration as applicable, enroll employees with the competent social-security bodies, and maintain accounting books and annual approval records.
required_dossiers: Employment and payroll registrations, if employees are hired
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct rejected tax or social registrations through the relevant portal, submit missing supporting evidence, and document all officer and shareholder approvals in the corporate records.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No general industrial licensing board is required for ordinary FPV racing or hobby drone assembly. The relevant authorities are the Prefect of the department, the Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL), and the Direction générale de l'aviation civile (DGAC) for aviation-related operator obligations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general manufacturing operating licence. An Installation Classée pour la Protection de l'Environnement (ICPE) declaration, registration, or authorization may be required if the facility or processes meet applicable ICPE nomenclature thresholds, including metalworking, surface treatment, combustion, storage, solvents, or hazardous substances.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition, acting through the relevant Prefecture and DREAL; environmental-authority review may be conducted by the Conseil général de l'environnement et du développement durable where applicable.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally exempt from a project-level full EIA for small-scale assembly and milling unless screening thresholds are met. An ICPE declaration, registration, or authorization assessment is required where the premises or process falls within the applicable ICPE nomenclature.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with the applicable ICPE order, local prefectural requirements, Water Act rules, and municipal wastewater conditions. Do not discharge industrial wastewater without authorization. Segregate and track hazardous waste, oils, resins, solvents, batteries, and carbon-fiber waste through authorized channels. Control dust, VOCs, noise, and machining emissions using suitable extraction, filtration, storage, and maintenance measures. Apply extended producer responsibility and waste-battery rules where the company places electrical equipment, batteries, or packaging on the French market.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No single national pre-opening occupational clearance applies to ordinary SAS manufacturing premises. The operator must complete workplace risk assessment in the DUERP, provide machine guarding, electrical safety, ventilation, personal protective equipment, chemical risk controls, training, and occupational-health arrangements. Fire-safety systems, emergency exits, extinguishers, alarm arrangements, and electrical inspections must comply with the premises classification. An ERP safety opinion or opening authorization is required if the site receives the public. Structural, fire, and electrical inspections must be obtained where required by the building owner, insurer, labor rules, or local authority.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) of the Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle et numérique. Operative portals: impots.gouv.fr (tax filing, VAT returns, TVA intracommunautaire identification) and formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (Guichet Unique des formalités d'entreprises). Large-business VAT compliance is channeled through the Direction des grandes entreprises (DGE, for turnover above EUR 400 million); all other SAS taxpayers file with the local Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: File the SAS incorporation dossier with the Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), replacing the former Centre de Formalités des Entreprises (CFE); an SAS requires no minimum share capital. Step 2: INPI verifies the dossier and records the company at the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), generating the 9-digit SIREN code; INSEE then assigns a 14-digit SIRET number for each establishment. Step 3: DGFiP automatically allocates the TVA intracommunautaire number (format FR + 11 digits) through identification data transmitted by the Guichet Unique; no taxable transaction may occur before this number is effective. Step 4: A non-resident seller without a French establishment that is not covered by OSS or IOSS must apply directly to DGFiP using form Cerfa n°15755 (demande d'identification TVA en France), appoint a French fiscal representative where legally required, and obtain a French VAT number before any delivery of goods into France. The same registration activates the SIRENE database, the FEC (Fichier des Écritures Comptables) obligation, and the electronic filing channel (Espace Professionnel).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. An SAS is compulsorily subject to French corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés, IS) under Article 206(1) CGI at the entity level; there is no pass-through option analogous to a US check-the-box election. Territorial scope: resident SAS are taxed on worldwide profits, with foreign permanent establishment profits relieved under applicable tax treaties and allocated profits method; non-resident branches are taxed only on French-source profits. The standard IS headline rate is 25%, with a reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for SMEs whose turnover does not exceed EUR 7.63 million, a bracket normally available to a newly incorporated FPV drone retail SAS.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists. Available French statutory elections: (1) Fiscal integration (intégration fiscale) under Article 223 A CGI, available to a French parent holding at least 95% of its SAS subsidiaries, allowing group profit and loss consolidation via form Cerfa n°2095-FC; (2) Franchise en base de TVA under Article 293 B CGI, under which a goods seller with annual turnover up to EUR 85,000 may elect or waive the VAT simplification, although OSS and e-commerce obligations normally make VAT registration commercially mandatory; (3) option for the régime réel normal instead of the régime réel simplifié d'imposition for VAT instalments and filing cycles; (4) the 15% reduced IS rate on the first EUR 42,500 of profit is a statutory bracket, not an election; (5) anti-hybrid rules under Articles 212-III to 212-V CGI operate by statutory application and present no elective choice for a standard SAS.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms_note: Reserved for cross-border hybrid flow planning; the SAS classification under French law is not elective, and tax treaty benefits are claimed by filing the annual declaration and, where relevant, Form 2065-SD within the statutory corporate tax calendar.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA), governed by CGI Articles 256 to 303 and Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: 0 EUR for a resident French SAS; VAT identification is compulsory from incorporation and no general small-trader exemption exists for a manufacturing and retailing entity. For non-established sellers, intra-EU distance sales and cross-border B2C supplies are subject to the single EU-wide threshold of EUR 10,000 per calendar year, above which French VAT applies at destination through the Union One Stop Shop (OSS) scheme; imports of consignments valued at EUR 150 or less may be cleared under the Import One Stop Shop (IOSS) without separate French VAT registration. The former national EUR 35,000 French distance-selling threshold was abolished on 1 July 2021 by the EU e-commerce VAT package.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory structured electronic invoicing and e-reporting are being phased in under the French e-invoicing reform (successive Finance Acts, most recently Loi de finances pour 2024, Article 88). Published calendar: large enterprises and mid-sized companies must issue and receive electronic invoices from 1 September 2026; SMEs and micro-enterprises from 1 September 2027. A proposed 2025 legislative amendment would postpone these dates by approximately one year, so the definitive timetable must be verified against the Finance Law and DGFiP guidance in force at onboarding. All domestic B2B invoices must be exchanged in structured formats (Factur-X, UBL, CII) via a certified Partner Dematerialization Platform (PDP) or the public Portail Public de Facturation (PPF); PDPs connect to the PPF API layer and transmit e-reporting data on B2C transactions and payment flows. France does not apply per-invoice real-time fiscal stamping; enforcement relies on NF 525-certified cash register and point-of-sale software for retail sales (Article 88 of Law n°2016-1918), the annual FEC accounting file, and DGFiP data-mining of PDP and PPF streams.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating of exports under CGI Article 262-I-1° applies to FPV drone sales where: (i) title and risk pass to a non-EU buyer; (ii) the goods physically leave the EU customs territory, with dispatch occurring within 90 days from delivery and actual export generally within 12 months; (iii) the French SAS is the exporter named on the export customs declaration (DAU/EX-A); and (iv) authorized transport documentation substantiates arrival at destination. Ancillary services and digital add-ons supplied B2B to non-EU customers fall outside French VAT under the place-of-supply rule in Article 259-1 CGI (customer establishment rule). Intra-EU B2B deliveries are exempt only where the customer's valid French or other EU VAT ID is obtained and the EU sales list (DEB) is filed; retail B2C distance sales to EU final consumers are taxed at destination and declared through OSS. Input VAT attributable to exported goods remains fully creditable, creating a recurring VAT refund position for the drone manufacturer.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU/EX-A, Electronic Export Accompanying Document)
Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill or postal CN23 despatch note for courier exports)
Inward Remittance Certificate proving foreign-currency settlement through a French intermediary
Commercial invoice with Incoterms and export sale contract or purchase order
Exporter's transport and tracking evidence (carrier manifest, delivery confirmation at destination)
Export transaction register (journal des exportations) reconciling each zero-rated invoice to its customs entry
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP subjects zero-rated export chains to documentary inspection; any missing or inconsistent DAU, Bill of Lading, or inward remittance file causes recharacterization as a domestic taxable sale, with full 20% VAT reassessed plus intérêts de retard (0.2% per month) and penalties under Article 1729 CGI of 40% for bad faith or 80% for abusive manipulation or fraud. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within the 180-day benchmark supports the administrative presumption that the export sale never materialized. Customs consequences under the Code des douanes include fines of one to three times the value of the goods (up to five times for false declaratory maneuvers) and confiscation of the goods and means of transport, as well as suspension or revocation of authorized exporter status. Criminal exposure arises under Article 1741 CGI and customs fraud provisions, with imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to EUR 500,000, increased for organized fraud. The statutory VAT reassessment period is generally three years (LPF Article L.169), extended to six years for undisclosed activity and up to ten years where fraudulent maneuvers are established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) with prudential licensing and AML/CTF supervision delegated to the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR); foreign-exchange regulatory competence is framed by the Code monétaire et financier (CMF) and exercised under the Treasury's policy direction (Direction Générale du Trésor, Ministère de l'Économie); TRACFIN serves as the French financial intelligence unit for suspicious cross-border transaction reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France maintains full euro convertibility on both current and capital accounts pursuant to Décret n°89-938 (29 December 1989), the OECD Codes of Liberalisation and TFEU Articles 63-66; no prior FX licensing, quotas or allocation systems apply to a French SAS. Current-account operations (trade settlement, service fees, royalties, licensing) are entirely free. Capital-account transactions for an inbound non-resident shareholder are free except for: (i) foreign direct investment screening under CMF Articles R151-3 et seq. that applies only to listed sensitive activities (defence, security, certain dual-use and critical technologies) - ISIC 3240 hobby racing drone manufacture is outside that list; (ii) dividend withholding tax on profit remittances to non-resident shareholders at the domestic rate (25% for corporate recipients, reduced by applicable double tax treaty; 12.8% plus social levies regime for individuals), which is a tax mechanism, not an FX restriction; (iii) financial sanctions and asset-freeze regimes (EU/UN consolidated lists) which may block payments to designated counterparties. No balance-of-payments approval is required for capital injection or dividend distribution; banks automatically report cross-border flows to Banque de France under its statistical collection duty.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. France abolished compulsory surrender, forced conversion and repatriation timelines for export proceeds in 1989. An FPV drone exporter may retain export earnings in EUR or in a foreign-currency account (compte en devises) indefinitely, convert them at will, and use them for onward supplier payments without statutory deadline or mandatory conversion ratio. For non-EU-currency receivables, the collecting French bank reports the transaction to Banque de France under its balance-of-payments statistical obligation; the exporter has no separate filing duty for routine trade flows. Export receipts linked to sanctioned destinations, or inconsistent with the underlying customs value, may trigger TRACFIN reporting and bank-side suspension.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High operational viability for ACPR-/PSD2-regulated electronic money institutions (Qonto, Shine, Manager.one, Wise Platform, Revolut Business) for daily treasury, Stripe/PayPal payout collection, multi-currency IBANs and remote onboarding of a French SAS. Legal constraints: (i) an EMI is not a credit institution and cannot issue the attestation de dépôt des fonds required by French corporate law for the share capital subscription - the statutory escrow must be opened with a licensed bank or the Caisse des Dépôts; (ii) EMI client funds are safeguarded in segregated accounts but are not covered by the FGDR EUR 100,000 deposit guarantee; (iii) EMIs often cap high-velocity supplier payments (typically EUR 100k/month) and offer no FX hedging products; (iv) multi-currency virtual IBANs are welcome for receivable collection but should not be used for capital injections to preserve audit and BOP traceability.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Tier-1 French banks generally mandate an in-person KYC interview of the SAS legal representative (Président) at a French branch; remote opening is available for some digital-first offers at BNP Paribas and Société Générale and for most EMIs, subject to eIDAS-qualified electronic signature, video-identification, and a French registered-office address (domiciliation). Non-resident directors must provide an apostilled/legalised passport, 3-month proof of address, corporate registry extracts with chain of UBOs, and audited or accountant-certified financials of the shareholder where relevant. A full remote opening without any French Nexus is not permitted; a power of attorney is accepted only after primary identity verification of the principal. Onboarding timelines: 2-4 weeks for Tier-1 banks, 3-7 days for EMIs, assuming clean sanctions screening and complete UBO documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Product line flagged as dual-use UAV/drone by the transaction-monitoring or sanctions engine despite ISIC 3240 toy classification, blocking account opening or freezing trade payables.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Evidence bundle: (a) binding customs classification note or prior tariff ruling placing the goods under CN code 9503.00 (toys and games) rather than CN 8806 (unmanned aircraft); (b) technical data sheet proving characteristics below EU Dual-Use Regulation 2021/821 Annex I thresholds (maximum take-off mass, endurance, top speed, absence of autonomous waypoint navigation, no precision-guided payload or thermal/EO camera, no low-observable design); (c) EU Declaration of Conformity under Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC and CE/RoHS/REACH certificates; (d) supplier composition declarations showing non-military-grade controllers and motors; (e) written dual-use classification opinion by EU counsel if any Annex I attribute is arguable; (f) end-user/end-use statement template for component imports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High concentration of cross-border payables to unincorporated Shenzhen/Guangdong component vendors triggering high-risk-jurisdiction and supplier due-diligence escorts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Evidence bundle: (a) legalised business licence and articles of association for the top 10 suppliers; (b) three-way match package (purchase order, proforma invoice, bank statement) for each disbursement; (c) EU SAD customs export/import declarations and air waybills naming the French SAS as consignee; (d) completed vendor due-diligence questionnaire with beneficial ownership declarations; (e) Incoterms 2020 contract matrix and international sale contracts; (f) product conformity certificates (CE, RoHS2, REACH) and records of customs clearance reconciliations; (g) shared-compliance letter describing open-book purchasing and annual supplier audit rights.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership: non-resident shareholder with layered holding structure, or capital subscription accepted without convincing source-of-funds explanation, triggering RBE/UBO verification backlog.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Evidence bundle: (a) Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) filing certified by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; (b) corporate organisational chart with exact share percentages and voting rights; (c) UBO passport and utility bill notarised or apostilled; (d) source-of-wealth file comprising 3-year shareholder financial statements, tax returns or employment/investment records; (e) Europol/Interpol and EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions screening confirmation dated at onboarding; (f) capital-subscription funds path demonstrable through the originating bank's SWIFT MT103 and bank confirmation letter addressed to the French settlement bank; (g) sworn declaration of no PEP status or disclosed PEP relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce refund and chargeback velocity through Stripe/PayPal flagged as ML flow-back or shadow-capital movement by the bank's detection engine.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Evidence bundle: (a) Stripe/PayPal platform settlement reports reconciled monthly against commercial invoices and proof-of-delivery (tracked AWB); (b) published refund, warranty and 14-day EU withdrawal policy compliant with Consumer Rights Directive 2011/83/EU; (c) 3-D Secure (payer authentication) logs for card transactions; (d) chargeback-ratio history (target below 0.9%) and merchant-of-record contracts for each platform; (e) appointed AML compliance officer under Article L561-1 CMF with appointment letter in the SAS compliance file; (f) annual revenue projection and treasury cash-flow plan demonstrating commercial consistency of transaction velocity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (1) open the blocked capital-subscription account (compte bloqué) at BNP Paribas or Société Générale using the Kbis extract, statutes, UBO dossier and board resolution approving the capital increase; (2) the non-resident shareholder remits via SWIFT MT103 for non-EUR currencies or SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR, with remittance information reading 'VERSEMENT CAPITAL SOCIAL - AUGMENTATION DE CAPITAL - SAS <SIREN>' and the bank's designated ISO 20022 purpose code for equity subscription (commonly 'EQUI' or the bank's own direct-investment menu code); (3) for remittances above EUR 15,000 from non-EEA counterparties, the collecting bank automatically files the Banque de France balance-of-payments statistical declaration (operation type F5111 - direct investment equity); no client-side declaration is required; (4) the bank issues the attestation de dépôt des fonds (depositary certificate) under Articles L227-1 and L227-9 of the French Commercial Code, which the notary or registrar requires; (5) after share issuance and filing at the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, the escrow is released to the operational account; (6) verify that the inbound investment does not fall under the CMF R151-3 FDI screening list - toy-grade FPV drones are outside it, but a written classification memo should be retained; (7) if the remittance is in USD or CNY, execute a spot or forward conversion with the bank and retain the FX confirmation and the MT103 for audit; never commingle capital injection with trade receivables in the same wire.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: EU supplier payments: SEPA Credit Transfer (EUR) cleared same-day via SEPA rails at zero cross-border premium under EU Regulation 2021/1230. Non-EU supplier payments: SWIFT MT103 with Field 70 purpose code 'TRAD' referencing the purchase order and commercial invoice; for Chinese component suppliers, settle in EUR on the supplier's EUR account or execute a bank-side EUR/CNY conversion with SWIFT MT103 RMB instruction; the RMB CIPS corridor is available at BNP Paribas for dedicated RMB flows, but EUR-invoiced terms are preferred to minimise conversion friction. Large or first-time Chinese vendors: documentary letters of credit under UCP600 issued via SWIFT MT700, sight payment against air waybill and commercial invoice; confirmation recommended for amounts above EUR 100,000; a 50% advance / 50% against-document structure is standard for drone-component purchasing. Stripe and PayPal payouts are received on the operational EUR account and swept daily or weekly to the main treasury account via SEPA Instant; card platforms must not be used to disburse supplier funds - platform balances can be withdrawn only to the verified SAS bank account, preserving the audit trail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (contrats à terme de change) on EUR/CNY, EUR/USD and EUR/HKD with an ACPR-licensed credit institution under CMF Article L211-1, maturities up to 12 months, documented under the bank's standard ISDA/FX master or treasury framework agreement.
FX swaps (swap de change) for same-day and next-day conversion of USD and CNY trade inflows into EUR, including tomorrow-next rolling structures.
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (EUR/USD, EUR/CNY) permissible where the SAS holds a corresponding working-capital facility and the hedge matches underlying exposure.
European-style FX options (EUR/USD, EUR/CNY) via the bank's derivatives desk under ISDA Master Agreement, with premium paid upfront and no retail leverage.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted only for pairs involving a non-deliverable underlying currency (e.g., EUR/IDR, EUR/PHP); EUR/CNY is a fully deliverable pair, so an NDF is neither required nor standard for the France-China corridor; retail FX hedging via Stripe, PayPal or unlicensed platforms is prohibited.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual approval of financial statements by the shareholders and recording of the deliberative decision
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate minutes book of the SAS; no separate filing to a government agency unless the accounts are deposited with the annual filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end; for a calendar-year SAS, approval must occur by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil liability of the president for failure to call the meeting; judicial intervention possible at shareholder request; the annual accounts cannot be validly filed without the approval decision.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory accounts filing at the commercial and companies register (depot des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the company's registered-office court
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two months after shareholder approval and no later than seven months after financial year-end; calendar-year SAS generally files by 31 August
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Compulsory filing order by the tribunal president after an eight-day formal notice, final daily penalty payments, possible reference to the public prosecutor, and procedural bar on deliveries of RCS certified extracts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale form 2065-SD with annexes including transfer-pricing declaration and salary-related forms)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — Service des Impôts des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a fiscal year ending 31 December: by 3 May of the following year; for a non-calendar fiscal year: within three months of the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic 10% late-filing penalty, increased to 40% after a formal notice remains ineffective; 0.3% per-month late-payment interest; possible discretionary tax reassessment without time limit.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business property tax declaration and settlement (cotisation foncière des entreprises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Declaration form 1447-C-SD due by 15 September of the taxation year; outstanding tax due by 15 December unless paid by monthly direct debit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10% plus statutory interest; late-payment surcharge of 5% after a 30-day notice; execution measures against movable goods.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial-owner declaration update in the RCS file when any shareholding or ultimate-ownership transfer occurred
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce through the Infogreffe electronic pipeline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of a qualifying ownership change; no separate annual filing is required if the beneficial-owner data remains unchanged, but the register must be reviewed and confirmed at the annual accounts approval meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False or deficient declaration punishable by criminal fines and imprisonment on repeat offence; failure to update prevents lawful use of the company's RCS file for contractual third-party verification.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An SAS must appoint a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) if it exceeds, for a financial year, at least two of the following thresholds: total balance sheet above €4.0 million, net turnover above €8.0 million, or 50 average employees; audit is also mandatory on shareholder request or by court order, and remains advisable for entities financing through external lenders.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual statutory annual accounts are prepared under French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général and ANC regulations); IFRS as adopted by the European Union is used for consolidated financial statements where the entity belongs to an IFRS-reporting group.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The president must maintain a complete and up-to-date register of beneficial owners at the registered office. The register is reviewed annually when the annual accounts are approved; if a share transfer changes the direct or indirect ownership chain by 10% or more or causes a change in control, an updated beneficial-owner declaration is filed with the Greffe within one month. No standalone annual UBO filing is otherwise due, but the register must always be available for Tracfin and judicial authorities.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members and share-transfer movements
Register of Directors and corporate officers
Minute Book of annual shareholder decisions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 – 1,100 per year for legal domiciliation and registered-office services in commercial cities
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,800 – 12,500 per year for a small to medium-size SAS

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax rate; reduced 15% rate applies to the first EUR 38,120 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs with annual turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Research Tax Credit (CIR) at 30% for eligible R&D expenditure up to EUR 100 million and 5% above the cap; Innovation Tax Credit for SMEs; preferential depreciation and a 5-year loss carryforward scheme applied in this dossier; territoriality exemption for foreign branch profits; anti-deferred financing deduction for SMEs under specific conditions

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: French liasse fiscale: Form 2065-SD and annexes 2050–2059-G; mandatory electronic filing via EFI portal (efi.impots.gouv.fr) or certified EDI-TDFC software
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly corporate income tax instalment payments are required for the following tax year, with a balance-settlement payment after filing
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year SAS, the annual return must be filed by the second working day following 1 May. For a non-calendar fiscal year, the return is due within 3 months of the fiscal year-end. A provisional first-year return or a cessation return is due under separate shortened deadlines.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet presenting assets, liabilities, shareholders' equity, provisions and intercompany receivables/payables.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only French SAS assets and liabilities; exclude foreign head-office assets and intra-group balances unless effectively attributable to the French business.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income statement summarising turnover from FPV drone retail, cost of goods sold, administrative expenses, depreciation and financial result.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognise only French-source revenue and DTA-apportioned income; avoid booking offshore sales and separate foreign principal income to the SAS unless supported by a French PE analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation from accounting profit to taxable result: add-backs for disallowed expenses, non-deductible CVAE charges, thin capitalisation interest and transfer pricing adjustments; deduct loss carryforward utilisation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the French thin-capitalisation safe harbours to loans from foreign shareholders and provide transfer pricing documentation if material related-party transactions exist.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Main corporation tax computation including reduced-rate declaration, ordinary corporation tax, social contribution surcharge if applicable, and balance payable after prior instalments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the French SIREN number, registered office, and the shareholding percentage of non-resident shareholders; attach a DTA residence certificate when treaty reductions are relied on.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Small-company reduced-rate schedule confirming eligibility for the 15% rate on the first EUR 38,120 of profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owned SAS will qualify only where the direct or ultimate shareholders are individuals or eligible entities under Article 219 CGI; a foreign corporate shareholder owning 75% or more may disqualify the reduced rate or require a DTA analysis.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an automatic 10% increase in the net corporate income tax; 40% is levied when filing occurs after a formal notice; 80% applies for deliberately fraudulent omissions. Late-payment interest accrues at 0.20% per month (2.4% per annum). Failure to use mandatory e-filing is separately sanctioned under Article 1738 CGI, with fines scaled by turnover and gravity.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% statutory withholding tax under Article 119 bis CGI on dividends distributed by a French SAS to non-resident shareholders, unless reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or a lower treaty rate is available.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain reduced withholding at source, the non-resident beneficial owner must provide the paying French SAS with a duly completed Form 5001 (corporate residence certificate) or Form 5000 (individual certificate), together with a beneficial-ownership attestation. Where the tax was already withheld, a reimbursement claim may be submitted under the Article 242-0 M CGI procedure, supported by an original tax residence certificate issued by the foreign tax authority, generally within the statutory time bar ending on 31 December of the second calendar year following the withholding event.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for IP use carry a domestic withholding rate of 33.33%; the EU Interest & Royalties Directive eliminates WHT for qualifying associated EU companies; French tax treaties commonly provide 0% for patent royalties and 0%–15% for trademark, copyright and know-how royalties, subject to beneficial ownership. Arm's-length debt interest paid to ordinary treaty residents is generally exempt from French withholding, while interest recharacterised as profit distribution may face 30% withholding; payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions are denied deduction and penalised.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400 million in annual revenue or balance-sheet total triggers mandatory French Master File and Local File documentation; consolidated groups with EUR 750 million or more in group revenue trigger Country-by-Country Reporting. For a smaller FPV drone e-commerce SAS, contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation is nevertheless prudent when related-party purchases or royalties exceed a de minimis threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not apply the Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR), but effectively requires the same substance through French tax-residence, permanent establishment, beneficial ownership, and general anti-abuse doctrines. A French SAS must have a genuine office, employees, management control and substantive operational decision-making in France to preserve its tax residence and to defend treaty benefits on repatriated profits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of PayPal and Stripe sales proceeds from FPV drone retail, creation of fictitious supplier invoices for carbon-fibre components, destruction of sales records, or concealment of cryptocurrency payment conversion and stock.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 1741 CGI imposes a criminal fine of EUR 500,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years on conviction; this rises to EUR 1,000,000 and 7 years for organised tax fraud. Civil penalties include an 80% increase in reassessed tax for fraudulent manipulation, plus late-payment interest at 2.4% per annum.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who personally sign false returns, issue false accounting documents, or knowingly organise concealment are jointly and severally liable for the company's tax, penalties and interest; criminal conviction additionally exposes them to travel bans, civil rights restrictions, asset freezing and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company and artificial tax avoidance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the French SAS as a letterbox that invoices EU retail sales while procurement, stockholding, product engineering and management decisions occur abroad, thereby avoiding a French permanent establishment or treaty abuse.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax administration may invoke abuse of law under Article L.64 LPF, impose an 80% penalty on the reassessed corporate tax, recharacterise the foreign hand-off as a French PE, and deny dividend, royalty or interest treaty protection.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a fictitious SAS may be personally liable for corporate tax and penalties where the veil is pierced; foreign directors may face French travel or entry restrictions during judicial procedures and can be personally prosecuted for criminal tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing manipulation and documentation failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Inflating intercompany purchase prices for motors and carbon-fibre parts, under-invoicing the FPV drone export to a related offshore distributor, or allocating residual marketing and R&D profit to low-tax jurisdictions without arm's-length benchmarking.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax administration can make a transfer pricing adjustment to the French SAS taxable profit, collect 2.4% annual interest, and apply a 40% penalty for lack of good faith. Failure to produce required transfer pricing documentation after formal request results in a EUR 50,000 fine, rising to EUR 100,000 after 30 days; CbCR non-compliance separately attracts sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign intercompany contracts knowing them to lack economic substance, or who make financial declarations without honest review, may be jointly liable for the recovery of unpaid tax where the company is left unable to pay; fraud-type transfer pricing conduct can also be prosecuted as criminal tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and beneficial ownership compliance breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing high-volume e-commerce payments through PayPal and Stripe while knowingly failing to identify ultimate shareholders, refusing to file or update the French beneficial-ownership register (RBE), or using layer-cake foreign shell companies to obscure ownership of the FPV drone retail operation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Breaches of the French Monetary and Financial Code may trigger administrative fines, compliance injunctions, and criminal penalties of up to 5 years' imprisonment and EUR 375,000 for individuals; directors can be personally held as beneficial owners for failure to disclose, without prejudice to money-laundering penalties applied to the SAS.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who hold or control the SAS and deliberately conceal beneficial ownership face personal fines, imprisonment, asset freezing and, where the company is a mere vehicle for money laundering, unlimited recovery against personal assets under civil forfeiture rules.
